content.content:
Models suite loses the server log when ollama37 runs outside compose
The models suite runs each test against the `ollama37` container and keeps that container's server log per test, for the report and the agent judge. A host that only runs model tests starts that container from a systemd unit, pinned to one card, instead of from `docker/docker-compose.yml`. The log collector only reads compose: `docker compose logs --follow` runs in `<repo>/docker`, so it sees only containers compose started from that folder, and the session stream holds nothing but the test markers. Its fallback, `docker logs ollama37`, is hard-coded to the name `ollama37`, so any other container name loses the server log entirely. Following the container's log by name, not through compose, with the name set in one place, lets the suite keep its logs however the container was started.

Context: [`.sessions/cf5a3839-e080-4036-9e9c-69476f9a0c27.jsonl`](../blob/main/.sessions/cf5a3839-e080-4036-9e9c-69476f9a0c27.jsonl)

## Where

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Stream: `docker compose logs --follow --timestamps`, `cwd` = `<repo>/docker` | `cicd/tests/src/log-collector.ts:72-76` |
| Reconnect: same command with `--since 1s` | `cicd/tests/src/log-collector.ts:177-181` |
| Fallback: `docker logs ollama37 --since … --until …` | `cicd/tests/src/log-collector.ts:417-419` |
| `dockerComposePath` = `<repo>/docker` handed to the collector | `cicd/tests/src/cli.ts:50,73` · `cicd/tests/src/executor.ts:283-286` |

## Done When

- [ ] A models-suite run against an `ollama37` container started outside compose writes the server log into each `<outputDir>/TC-*.log` and `session.log`.
- [ ] The container name the collector follows is set in one place.
- [ ] A run on a compose-started container (the K80 host) still writes the same logs.

name: Identify host
description: >
  Record which self-hosted runner and which GPUs a job actually ran on, into the step
  summary and the log. Makes every result attributable to a specific testbed instead of
  "self-hosted".

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      run: |
        set -u

        if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          # `compute_cap` is not a valid query field on older nvidia-smi — notably the 470
          # branch that drives the K80, which is the reference testbed. Probe for it and
          # drop it rather than failing the job on every workflow.
          fields="name,compute_cap,memory.total,driver_version"
          if ! nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap --format=csv,noheader >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            fields="name,memory.total,driver_version"
          fi

          # A host with the driver installed that cannot be queried is a broken host, not
          # a CPU host. Reporting "none detected" there would silently strip attribution
          # from the result — the same reason gpu-temp-guard.sh aborts on unreadable polls.
          # stderr goes to a file, never into the parsed output: a benign nvidia-smi
          # warning must not be mistaken for a GPU row.
          err="$(mktemp)"
          if ! smi="$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu="${fields}" --format=csv,noheader 2>"$err")" \
             || [ -z "${smi:-}" ]; then
            # nvidia-smi reports an unusable query on stdout, not stderr. Print both, or
            # the reason for the failure is invisible.
            echo "identify-host: nvidia-smi returned no usable output for '${fields}'." >&2
            echo "--- stdout ---" >&2; printf '%s\n' "${smi:-}" >&2
            echo "--- stderr ---" >&2; cat "$err" >&2
            rm -f "$err"
            exit 1
          fi
          rm -f "$err"
          mapfile -t gpus <<< "${smi}"

content.text:
**IN FLIGHT**: the design for #513 is worked out, but I haven't changed any code yet. The deciding fact: keep `ollama37` on port `11434` as a fixed contract on every host, and put what differs per host in each runner's own `.env`. Then no GitHub variable is needed, and host A keeps working unchanged at the same time.

**Finding:**
- The hardcode goes further than the log collector. All 19 model testcases call `docker exec ollama37` (45 times) or `docker inspect ollama37` (2 times), and all 19 use `localhost:11434`. Making those configurable would touch every YAML.
- Host B has **no runner registered** on GitHub. Only `rocky8-k80-cicd-1` (host A, label `sm37`, currently offline) exists. The `rocky9-2060-cicd-1` unit here is a leftover.
- `test-models.yml` has **no `concurrency:` group**, so two runs on two runners already work in parallel.
- `/opt/actions-runner/.env` on this host already sets `GPU_TEMP_LIMIT`. A per-host runner `.env` is a pattern the repo already uses.

## Design, bottom up

**1. Hardcode: make the name a contract, not a variable**

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| Host B's systemd unit | `--name ollama37` (instead of `ollama`), still on 11434 |
| `log-collector.ts` stream and reconnect | `docker logs --follow --timestamps ollama37` instead of `docker compose logs`. On host A the compose container is also named `ollama37`, so both hosts behave the same. |
| `log-collector.ts` fallback | uses the same name, from one constant: `OLLAMA37_CONTAINER`, default `ollama37` (Done When #2) |
| 19 testcases | untouched |

One side effect to fix: `docker logs` sends the server's stderr to stderr, so the collector would prefix most lines with `[stderr] `. No parser depends on that prefix, but the logs would look different from host A's.

**2. Running part of the model tests on host B**

Add a filter to `cli.ts` read from an env var, for example `MODELS_TEST_IDS=TC-MODELS-003,…`. Unset means run everything. Host B's runner `.env` lists the 12 tests that fit on one card, from `single-gpu-load-test.md`. Host A's `.env` doesn't set it, so it keeps running all 19.

**3. Host A at the same time**

| Option | Host A affected? | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Runner `.env` per host** | No: each runner's `.env` only reaches its own jobs | One file on host B |
| GitHub environment per host (`cicd-1` / `cicd-2`) | Needs `environment:` picked by label in each workflow | Workflow edits, plus a second set of variables |
| Repository variable | Yes: it's shared, so it would apply to host A too | — |

Dispatch one run per label, e.g. `-f runner_label=sm37` and `-f runner_label=<host-B label>`. They run side by side; artifacts are stored per run, so they don't clash.

**Recommend:** runner `.env` plus the fixed name contract. One question is still open. Host B has two cards but one `ollama37` slot, so a single runner there can't tell which card the active unit is pinned to. Either register one runner and use a label that doesn't name a card, or accept a card label that is only true while that card's unit is running.

**Next step:** decide how host B's runner is labelled. After that I'll implement the two code changes (log collector and ID filter) on a branch and verify with a real run of TC-MODELS-003 on this host before opening a PR. Registering the runner needs a token from GitHub, so you'd run that part.

content.text:
Your first point changes the design. The agent judge is **host B's own `ollama.service`**: `JUDGE_BASE_URL` points at this machine on :11434, with `JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-oss-64k:20b`. That model is 13.8 GB, which doesn't fit one card, so the judge needs **both GPUs**. It therefore excludes every ollama37 test service on host B, and not only on the port.

## What that breaks

| Conflict | Why |
|---|---|
| One host B job needs two services | `cli.ts run` runs every test first (line 142), then judges all of them (line 175). The tests need `ollama37-<card>` up and the judge down; judging needs the reverse. |
| Host A needs host B's judge | A host A run in dual mode calls host B's judge during its judge phase. If host B is testing at that moment, the judge is down. |
| The `BindsTo=` runner units I wrote | A job that stops `ollama37-<card>` would kill its own runner mid-job. The binding has to go. |
| Two runners on host B | Two jobs at once could each flip services and break each other. |

## 3. Yes, add a step that controls the service, as a host hook

Following your rule that the logic lives in the script and the config lives on the host:
- **Script:** `cli.ts` runs `$OLLAMA37_BEFORE_TESTS` before the tests, and `$OLLAMA37_AFTER_TESTS` after them, before judging. The after-hook also runs on failure.
- **Host B's runner `.env`:**
  ```
  OLLAMA37_BEFORE_TESTS=systemctl --user stop ollama && systemctl --user start ollama37-3060
  OLLAMA37_AFTER_TESTS=systemctl --user stop ollama37-3060 && systemctl --user start ollama
  ```
- **Host A** doesn't set either variable, so nothing changes there.
- **Judge client:** waits (with a timeout) until `JUDGE_BASE_URL` answers. A host A run that reaches its judge phase during host B's test window then waits instead of failing.

## 2. Revised switching on host B

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| You bring an `ollama37-<card>` unit up and down by hand | The job does it through the hooks; by default `ollama.service` (the judge) is up |
| Two runners, each bound to a unit | **One runner** on host B, labelled `sm61` and `sm86`. It runs one job at a time, so host B work is serialized without a lock. |
| Card fixed per runner | Card picked per job: the workflow passes `runner_label`, and the hook maps `sm61` → `ollama37-1080ti`, `sm86` → `ollama37-3060`. The container name and test IDs follow the same mapping. |

The runner has to be a **user** service (as prepared) so the job can run `systemctl --user`. `ollama.service` needs to stay enabled so the judge comes back after a reboot.

**Recommend:** the hook design with one host B runner. Two things in it need your decision:
- **The judge's wait timeout.** Too short and a host A run fails during a long host B window; too long and a real outage goes unnoticed for that long.
- **Card choice.** Card-per-label means `.env` can't hold a single container name. Either the hook exports it per card, or each card gets its own small env file that the hook loads.

**Next step:** tell me whether to go with this. If so, I'll first remove the `BindsTo=`/`Wants=` bindings I added to the units. I'll leave the die-check problem (pid 5813) as a separate item.

Yes, that works, with the ollama37 units and the runners fully separate (no `BindsTo`/`Wants`). One ordering problem has to be solved first: **the judge runs inside the same test step**.

## The dynamic flow in `test-models.yml`

```
Checkout / setup (as now)
      │
      ▼
[new] Yield GPU                      runs only if the host's .env sets OLLAMA37_SERVICE
      ├─ systemctl --user is-active ollama ?
      │     yes → stop ollama, record restore=true
      │     no  → record restore=false
      └─ start $OLLAMA37_SERVICE → wait for /api/tags
      ▼
Run models tests  (execute only, no judge)
      ▼
[new] Restore GPU     if: always()
      ├─ stop $OLLAMA37_SERVICE
      └─ restore=true → start ollama → wait for /api/tags
      ▼
[new] Agent judge     reads the saved results; the judge (ollama) is back up
      ▼
Check results / unload / upload (as now)
```

Host A doesn't set `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, so the two new steps do nothing there and its run is unchanged. "Dynamic" means the job only restarts `ollama` if it was running when the job began.

## What has to change for that

| Need | Why | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Judge after the restore | Today `cli.ts run` runs the tests and then judges (lines 142 → 175) in one step. With `ollama` down, the judge would fail. | Run tests with `JUDGE_MODE=simple`, then a new `cli.ts judge <results dir>` step runs the agent judge on the saved results |
| Service names outside the workflow | Keeps the logic in the pipeline and the config on the host | Runner `.env`: `OLLAMA37_SERVICE=ollama37-3060`, `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE=ollama` |
| `systemctl --user` from the job | The job has to reach your user systemd | The runner runs as a **user** service (already prepared, lingering is on) |
| Host A's judge during host B's test window | Host B's judge is down for those minutes | The judge client waits (with a timeout) for `JUDGE_BASE_URL` instead of failing |

## One conflict left: two runners on host B

A 1080 Ti job and a 3060 job at the same time would both claim port 11434, and the second job would find `ollama` already stopped, so it would record `restore=false`. The options:

1. **One runner on host B** with labels `sm61` and `sm86`. It runs one job at a time, so host B is serialized for free. The `.env` holds both mappings (`OLLAMA37_SERVICE_sm61=ollama37-1080ti`, `OLLAMA37_SERVICE_sm86=ollama37-3060`), and the step picks one by `runner_label`.
2. Two runners plus a host lock: the Yield step waits on a lock file that the Restore step releases.
3. Two runners and different ports, but you ruled out port changes.

**Recommend:** option 1. It needs the least code and the fewest moving parts.

**Next step:** confirm option 1 and the split into tests-then-judge. I'll then remove the `BindsTo`/`Wants` edits from the units and fold this into `fix-513-host-env`.

content.text:
**No, host B has no problem under those two rules.** Two jobs could only clash if they overlapped, and you won't run them at the same time. Two edge cases are still worth closing with a line each:

| Edge case | What happens | Cheap fix |
|---|---|---|
| The runner or host dies mid-job (reboot, kill) | The `always()` restore step never runs, so `ollama37-<card>` stays up and `ollama` stays down. The next job then sees `ollama` down, records `restore=false`, and never brings it back. | The Yield step first stops any `ollama37-*` unit left running. The Restore step starts `ollama` if it's **enabled**, not "if it was running". That self-heals after one job. |
| You start a second job by mistake | Port clash on 11434 | Nothing; accept it, since you're the only user |

A cancelled job is fine: `if: always()` steps still run when a job is cancelled.

## Host A needs nothing

| Item | Host A |
|---|---|
| `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` | not set → the Yield and Restore steps skip |
| Container, `OLLAMA_HOST`, test IDs | not set → defaults `ollama37`, `localhost:11434`, all tests |
| Server | compose-started `ollama37`, as today; the runtime suite still runs `compose down/up` |
| Tests-then-judge split | Same workflow, so host A also runs `JUDGE_MODE=simple` then the judge step. The result is the same as today, just split into two steps. |
| Runner `.env` | Nothing new. It keeps `GPU_TEMP_LIMIT` if set. |

**One real dependency remains:** host A's agent judge *is* host B's `ollama`. Any host A run in dual mode needs host B idle with `ollama` up. With one run at a time, that holds by itself. If you ever overlap them, host A's judge would fail during host B's test window. The fix would be for the judge to wait until `JUDGE_BASE_URL` answers.

**Recommend:** keep your two runners, add the two self-healing lines, and skip the judge wait for now.

**Next step:** say go, and I'll:
1. remove the `BindsTo`/`Wants` edits from the units;
2. add the Yield and Restore steps, the `cli.ts judge` step and the runner `.env` keys on `fix-513-host-env`;
3. verify with one real host B run.

## Revised solution

The fix grows from "follow the container by name" to **no host-specific value in the pipeline**. Each self-hosted runner's `.env` holds what differs per host. The script holds the logic and the defaults.

### 1. Host knobs, read from the runner's `.env`

| Knob | Default (host A needs nothing) | Host B (per card) |
|---|---|---|
| `OLLAMA37_CONTAINER` | `ollama37` | `ollama37-1080ti` / `ollama37-3060` |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | `http://localhost:11434` | default |
| `OLLAMA37_TEST_IDS` | unset, so every test | the testcases that load 100% on one card |
| `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` | unset, so no service switching | `ollama37-1080ti` / `ollama37-3060` |
| `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE` | unset | `ollama` (the agent-judge server, both cards) |

Code that uses them (on `fix-513-host-env`):
- `cicd/tests/src/config.ts` sets the defaults, once.
- The log collector follows `docker logs --follow $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER`, with no compose dependency.
- All suites' testcases use `$OLLAMA37_CONTAINER` and `$OLLAMA_HOST` (48 + 90 uses).
- Workflows drop the job-level `OLLAMA_HOST`, so the runner's `.env` wins.
- `docker-compose.yml` reads `container_name` from `OLLAMA37_CONTAINER`.

### 2. Host B switches its GPUs per job

Host B's main use is `ollama` on both cards, which is also the agent judge (`JUDGE_BASE_URL`). A model-test job borrows one card and gives it back:

```
Yield GPU     (only if OLLAMA37_SERVICE is set)
  stop any ollama37-* unit left running
  ollama active? → stop it
  start $OLLAMA37_SERVICE → wait for /api/tags
Run models tests       JUDGE_MODE=simple (execute only)
Restore GPU   if: always()
  stop $OLLAMA37_SERVICE
  ollama enabled? → start it → wait for /api/tags
Agent judge            cli.ts judge <results>, now that the judge is back
```

- Runners and ollama37 units are separate; there are no `BindsTo`/`Wants`. One runner per card, as user services, so a job can run `systemctl --user`.
- The Restore step starts `ollama` if it's *enabled*, not "if it was running". A job killed mid-run then heals on the next job.
- Tests before judge needs a new `cli.ts judge` subcommand. Today `cli.ts run` executes and judges in one process, while the judge's server is down.

### 3. Host A is unchanged

No new `.env` keys. The Yield and Restore steps skip, and the defaults match today's values. The only difference is that execute and judge become two steps.

### Constraints accepted

- **One job at a time on host B.** The 1080 Ti and 3060 runners would clash on port 11434; there's a single user, so this is by convention.
- **Host A's agent judge needs host B idle with `ollama` up.** Don't overlap a host A dual-judge run with a host B test window. If that ever matters, the judge client waits for `JUDGE_BASE_URL`.

### Open

- **The die check counts every compute process on the visible GPU.** On the GTX 1080 Ti, TC-MODELS-003 loaded fully (29/29 layers, logs captured through the new collector) but failed `GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED`: a second 99 MiB process sat on the card. The check also hard-codes the K80 die size, 11441 MiB.
- **Runner registration for host B is still to do.**

result: ${{ steps.models-tests.outcome }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Identify host
        uses: ./.github/actions/identify-host

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Install test runner dependencies
        run: cd cicd/tests && npm ci

      # Only on a host whose runner .env sets OLLAMA37_SERVICE: stop the host's own
      # server and bring up the one under test. Restore GPU below gives it back.
      - name: Yield GPU
        run: |
          [ -n "${OLLAMA37_SERVICE:-}" ] || { echo "No OLLAMA37_SERVICE on this host"; exit 0; }
          systemctl --user stop 'ollama37-*'
          if [ -n "${OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE:-}" ]; then systemctl --user stop "$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE"; fi
          systemctl --user start "$OLLAMA37_SERVICE"
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sf "${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://localhost:11434}/api/tags" >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 2; done
          echo "::error::$OLLAMA37_SERVICE did not come up"; exit 1

      - name: Run models tests
        id: models-tests
        env:
          # The agent judge runs in its own step, after Restore GPU.
          JUDGE_MODE: simple
        run: |
          cd cicd/tests
          echo "Judge mode: ${JUDGE_MODE}"

          # Build test ID flag if provided
          ID_FLAG=""
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.test_id }}" ]; then
            ID_FLAG="--id ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
            echo "Running single test: ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
          fi

          # Run models tests. No gpu-temp-guard: its 80°C abort killed full-suite runs
          # (35549667518, peak 81°C at case 9 of 19) while the K80 itself only slows at
          # 88°C and shuts down at 93°C. The card's own thresholds are the protection
          # here. A non-zero exit stays tolerated — the JSON below is the gate.
          npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models $ID_FLAG --output-dir ../results/models --format json > /tmp/models-results.json || true

          echo "--- JSON Results ---"
          cat /tmp/models-results.json

      - name: Unload test models from VRAM
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "Unloading test models from VRAM..."
          # Derived from the suite, so adding or removing a testcase needs no edit here.
          for m in $(grep -ohE '"model":"[^"]+"' cicd/tests/testcases/models/*.yml | cut -d'"' -f4 | sort -u); do
            curl -s ${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://localhost:11434}/api/generate -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"keep_alive\":0}" || true
          done
          echo "Models unloaded"

      - name: Restore GPU
        if: always()
        run: |
          [ -n "${OLLAMA37_SERVICE:-}" ] || exit 0
          systemctl --user stop "$OLLAMA37_SERVICE"
          [ -n "${OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE:-}" ] || exit 0
          # enabled, not "was running": a job killed mid-run heals on the next one
          systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet "$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE" || exit 0
          systemctl --user start "$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE"
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sf "${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://localhost:11434}/api/tags" >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 2; done
          echo "::error::$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE did not come back"; exit 1

      - name: Agent judge
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && (inputs.judge_mode || 'dual') == 'dual' }}
        env:
          JUDGE_MODE: dual
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          # JUDGE_BASE_URL (cicd-1 variable) points the judge at an ollama server
          # instead of Anthropic — a judge off the box under test. Unset it and
          # the judge falls back to Claude on the OAuth token above; the auth
          # token has to follow the base URL or it would break that fallback.
          ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL }}
          ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && 'ollama' || '' }}
          ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
          # Claude Code's side-call model; ollama has no haiku tag to serve it.
          ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
        run: |
          cd cicd/tests
          npx tsx src/cli.ts judge ../results/models --format json > /tmp/models-results.json || true
          cat /tmp/models-results.json

      - name: Check test results
        run: |
          FAILED=$(jq '.summary.failed' /tmp/models-results.json)
          echo "Failed tests: $FAILED"
          if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::$FAILED models test(s) failed"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Upload models results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: models-test-results
          path: |
            /tmp/models-results.json
            cicd/results/

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Yield GPU | stopped `ollama37-*` and `ollama`, started `ollama37-3060`; it answered on the 2nd try and sees only the RTX 3060 |
| Run (simple judge) | 4/4 steps pass, including the die check; 228 log lines captured from `ollama37-3060`; `results.json` saved |
| Unload + Restore GPU | `ollama37-3060` stopped; `ollama` (enabled) started again as the judge server |
| `cli.ts judge` | agent judge ran on host B's `ollama` using the `JUDGE_MODEL` from `cicd-1`: **PASS**, summary 1 passed / 0 failed |

**Finding:** the die check passes on the 3060, so the extra 99 MiB process is on the **GTX 1080 Ti only**. That's probably the display, since the 1080 Ti drives the screen. The 1080 Ti runner will fail `GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED` until the check ignores processes that aren't ollama's. That's still open.

## What changed

- **Branch `fix-513-host-env`** (40 files, uncommitted), on top of the earlier env work:
  - `cli.ts` saves `results.json`, and the judge-and-report block is now one function shared by `run` and the new `judge <dir>` command.
  - `test-models.yml` gets **Yield GPU**, then run (`JUDGE_MODE=simple`, `--output-dir ../results/models`), then Unload, then **Restore GPU** (`always()`), then **Agent judge** (`!cancelled()`, dual only), then Check and Upload.
- **Host B units:**
  - The `Wants`/`BindsTo`/`After` bindings are removed.
  - The runner units got `[Install] WantedBy=default.target`.
  - Each runner's `.env` got `OLLAMA37_SERVICE=ollama37-<card>` and `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE=ollama`.
  - `daemon-reload` is done, so the per-card container names are live.
- **State I changed on this host:** `ollama37-1080ti`, which you had started by hand, is now stopped. `ollama` is running again.

## Not done

- Runner registration and enabling. Registration was blocked for me, so you'd run:
  `cd ~/actions-runner-<card> && ./config.sh --unattended --url https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37 --token <token> --name rocky9-<card>-cicd-1 --labels sm61|sm86`,
  then `systemctl --user enable --now actions-runner-<card>`.
- The die-check fix for the 1080 Ti.
- A host A run. Its path only changes in that execute and judge are now two steps.
- No commit and no PR. Your memory rule says a PR needs a real model run; this run counts for host B, but host A hasn't been run.

**Recommend:** fix the die check before registering the 1080 Ti runner. Otherwise its first CI run fails on something unrelated to this change.

**Next step:** choose one: fix the die check next, or commit what's here now.

lines: -Enable Ollama to run on Tesla K80 GPUs (CUDA compute capability 3.7), which are no longer supported by mainstream Ollama builds. This requires custom compilation with CUDA 11.4 and legacy CUBLAS function fallbacks.
-The CI/CD pipeline runs on a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner with Tesla K80 hardware. This is necessary because:
-1. K80 requires specific NVIDIA driver (470.x) and CUDA version (11.4)
-2. Cloud runners don't provide legacy GPU hardware
-3. Real GPU testing is essential - emulation cannot catch CUBLAS compatibility issues
-The build uses a two-stage Docker approach:

-**Stage 1 (Builder)**: A cached base image containing the complete toolchain - Rocky Linux 8, CUDA 11.4, GCC 10 (compiled from source due to RHEL limitations), CMake, and Go. This image takes ~90 minutes to build but is reused across all builds.
-**Stage 2 (Runtime)**: Built on each commit, this stage clones the source, compiles with K80-specific CMake presets, and packages the binary. Build time is ~10 minutes.
-This separation means routine builds are fast while toolchain changes are rare and cached.
-The test framework is designed around two key insights:
-1. **Exit codes lie**: A CUDA operation can fail silently, returning success while producing garbage output. Traditional pass/fail based on exit codes misses these failures.
-2. **Logs tell truth**: The real story is in the execution logs - CUBLAS errors, memory allocation failures, and GPU fallback warnings appear there even when commands "succeed".
-**Simple Judge**: Fast, deterministic verification based on:
-- Pattern matching (expected patterns found, rejected patterns absent in output)
-- CUDA error detection (no CUBLAS/CUDA errors in logs)

-**Agent Judge**: Semantic analysis via the keyless ACP agent judge — a Claude agent over the Agent Client Protocol (no API key, no container). It receives test criteria + logs and evaluates whether the actual behavior matches the expected behavior. This catches:
-- CUDA errors that don't cause exit failures
-- Subtle GPU fallback to CPU mode
-**Dual Mode** (default): Both judges must pass. This combines the speed of simple checking with the depth of semantic analysis.
-A critical problem with container log analysis is temporal precision. Using `docker compose logs --since=5m` creates issues:
-- Logs from previous tests contaminate current test analysis
-- Long-running tests may exceed the time window
-- Fast tests include irrelevant historical logs
-The LogCollector solves this using a file-based architecture with embedded text markers.
-The session file contains all docker logs with embedded markers:
-- ISO_TIMESTAMP: When the marker was written
-# Extract logs for TC-RUNTIME-001 (excluding marker lines)
-For tests still running (no END marker yet), extraction continues to EOF:
-1. **Crash Resilience**: The session file persists at `/tmp/ollama37-session-{timestamp}.log` even if the test process crashes. This enables post-mortem log analysis.
-2. **Bounded Memory**: No in-memory array growth. All logs are written directly to disk.
-3. **Precise Boundaries**: Text markers provide exact test boundaries regardless of docker log buffering delays.
-4. **Race Condition Prevention**: All writes (both docker log data and markers) go through a serialized write queue with line buffering, ensuring markers never interleave with log lines.
-- Old session files (> 24 hours) are automatically cleaned up at LogCollector startup
-- Stale test log files are removed when a new test with the same ID starts
-1. **Load Phase**: YAML test definitions are parsed and sorted by dependency order
-2. **Collection Start**: LogCollector begins streaming container logs
-3. **Execution Phase**: Tests run sequentially, each step receiving current test ID via environment
-4. **Log Capture**: Before each step, accumulated logs are written to a test-specific file
-5. **Judgment Phase**: Both judges evaluate results - simple checks exit codes, LLM analyzes logs
-6. **Cleanup**: Models are unloaded from VRAM, log collector stops
-Tests are organized into four suites that must run in order:
-**Build Suite** (3 tests): Verifies the builder Docker image contents, runtime image build, and image-size invariants. No GPU required.

-**Runtime Suite** (4 tests): Starts the container and verifies GPU detection, container health, and `/api/metrics` endpoint schema. Critical validation that the driver/toolkit/container integration works.
-**Inference Suite** (2 tests): Tests model pull + API inference with gemma3:4b. Validates that models load correctly and generate responses using GPU.

-**Models Suite** (13 tests): Per-model regression coverage on K80 hardware — gpt-oss:20b, ministral-3:3b, gemma3 (4b / 27b), gemma4 (e4b / 26b), qwen3.5 (9b / 27b), qwen3-vl (8b / 30b), deepseek-r1 (14b / 32b). Each model size unloads after testing to free VRAM for the next.
-K80 has limited VRAM (12GB per GPU). The framework explicitly unloads each model after its tests complete, rather than relying on automatic eviction. This ensures:
-- Clean baseline for each model size test
-Workflow-level cleanup provides a safety net if individual test unloads fail.
-The framework specifically watches for K80-related failure patterns:
-- `CUBLAS_STATUS_*` errors indicate the legacy CUBLAS fallback isn't working
-- `id=cpu library=cpu` means GPU detection failed entirely
-These patterns are checked by both the simple judge (via grep in test steps) and the agent judge (via semantic log analysis).
-**Why YAML test cases?** Declarative test definitions separate test logic from execution machinery. Adding a new test requires no code changes.

-**Why LLM judging?** Traditional test assertions require anticipating every failure mode. LLM evaluation can recognize novel failures and evaluate fuzzy criteria like "response should mention Paris".
-**Why sequential execution?** Log collection with precise boundaries requires knowing which test is running. Parallel execution would interleave logs unpredictably.
-**Why Docker-based builds?** Reproducibility. The exact toolchain that works is captured in the builder image. No "works on my machine" issues.
-**Why self-hosted runners?** K80 hardware. No cloud provider offers compute capability 3.7 GPUs for CI/CD.
-- Tests must run sequentially for accurate log collection
-- The agent judge requires Claude auth on the runner (`~/.claude` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`)
-- K80 VRAM limits restrict maximum model size to ~27B parameters
-- Build times are significant due to CUDA compilation
-The test framework integrates with GitHub Actions via reusable workflows in `.github/workflows/`:
-Runs all test suites in sequence: build → runtime → inference → models. This is the primary workflow for full validation.
-- `test-inference.yml` — Inference suite (2 tests); supports `JUDGE_MODE=dual` opt-in agent judge
-- `test-models.yml` — Models suite (13 tests); supports `JUDGE_MODE=dual` opt-in agent judge
-- Individual TC workflows do not manage container lifecycle
-- Container must be running before runtime / inference / models tests
-- Pipeline workflow orchestrates the sequence via `needs:` dependencies
-- All workflows run on self-hosted runners with K80 hardware

-The TC framework above handles **correctness validation** — "did this model load and produce coherent output?". Performance benchmarks and experiments live alongside under a separate, simpler contract:
-- A TypeScript subcommand per workflow or experiment (`cli.ts bench-throughput`, `cli.ts test-mcp`)
-- Metrics + coherence judging reuse the framework's perf helpers and the one agent judge
-- A JSON report (`--output`) plus a markdown summary on stdout
-- Workflow manages container lifecycle (stop production → run → restart production → upload artifacts)

-Current perf workflows: `test-throughput.yml` (tok/s benchmark). The agent judge is invoked here too but only ever to answer "is this response meaningful for its prompt?" — never for static / log / exit-code checks.

-`cli.ts test-mcp` is a **capability** probe rather than a perf metric: it drives a **real** stdio MCP server (server-agnostic — default `testlink-mcp`, override via `--mcp-command`/`--mcp-args`), lists and translates its tools to Ollama's `/api/chat` `tools[]`, runs the model's tool loop against the live server, and reuses the one agent judge to grade whether the final answer is grounded in the tool result. It reports a per-model verdict (PASS / FAIL / NO TOOL SUPPORT) and runs via the manual `test-mcp.yml` workflow (`workflow_dispatch`; testlink-mcp creds supplied as `cicd-1` secrets and forwarded with `--mcp-env`). See [`docs/traces/mcp-tool-call-validation.md`](../../docs/traces/mcp-tool-call-validation.md) for an end-to-end validation run.

-`--verify-live` is the stronger check (supersedes `--judge`): instead of grading the model's answer over the captured trajectory, an independent keyless verifier **calls the server's read-only tools itself** and confirms the answer against the live result. Tool access is an exact, fail-closed allow-list (`--verify-allow list_projects`, `--verify-server-name testlink`) — anything not listed is denied, so the verifier can never write. To stop the operator's account connectors and this repo's `.claude/` from flooding the spawned agent's toolset and burying the injected server, the verifier runs the agent in a **permanent isolated config dir** (`~/.cache/ollama37-verify`, override `VERIFY_CONFIG_DIR`): built once, connectors off, the clean cwd pre-trusted, and `.credentials.json` symlinked to the live `~/.claude` token so auth stays fresh and keyless (in CI the token comes from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`). The captured live result is surfaced in the report's **Live evidence** column. If the verifier can't authenticate or start, the run fails closed rather than silently downgrading. Set `judge_mode: verify-live` in the workflow.
-# Also run the agent judge (default is simple judge only)

## README Structure Conventions (2026)

A high-converting GitHub README in 2026 has quick-start code in the first 200 words, demo GIFs, and a FAQ section. The median length is 800-1,500 words.

### Quick Start Best Practices

Give users a working example in under 30 seconds with the pattern: install, run one command, see output. If your quick start takes more than five steps, your onboarding needs simplifying.

Make installation a single copy-paste, list prerequisites with versions, and provide a minimal working example that must actually run against the current code.

### Folder Structure

Source files are usually stored inside the src folder, or alternatively into the lib folder if you're developing a library, or into the app folder if application source files are not supposed to be compiled.

Excellent READMEs share three properties: they are accurate (every command works, every example runs), they are scannable (readers can find installation, usage, and license in seconds).

## AGENTS.md Overview

AGENTS.md has become the de facto standard for instructing AI coding agents. AGENTS.md is a standardized markdown file at the root of a repository that gives AI coding agents instructions, context, and conventions for working in that codebase, functioning as a README written for LLMs: human-readable, but optimized for machine consumption and prescriptive enough to drive consistent agent behavior.

# cicd

Every ollama37 build is checked on real GPUs by YAML testcases that one TypeScript runner executes, locally or in GitHub Actions. The testbeds are no longer one K80 box: a second host shares its cards with the agent judge's server, and it can run only the tests that fit one card. A pipeline that hard-codes one container, one address and one test list cannot run there without breaking the host it runs on. So each self-hosted runner's `.env` names its own server under test, and the models workflow borrows a card and gives it back.

## Quick start

```bash
cd cicd/tests
npm ci
npx tsx src/cli.ts list                                   # every testcase
npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models --id TC-MODELS-003  # one test, simple judge
```

In CI:

```bash
gh workflow run test-models.yml -f runner_label=sm86 -f test_id=TC-MODELS-003
```

## 1. One runner, three layers

![Workflow picks a host by label, calls cli.ts, which runs the YAML testcases](../docs/diagrams/png/cicd-layers.png)

A workflow in `.github/workflows/test-*.yml` picks a self-hosted runner by `runner_label`. It calls `cicd/tests/src/cli.ts`, which runs the testcases in `cicd/tests/testcases/<suite>/TC-*.yml`. A testcase's steps are bash commands. A local run and a CI run call the same `cli.ts`.

| Workflow | Command |
|---|---|
| `test-build.yml` · `test-runtime.yml` · `test-inference.yml` · `test-models.yml` | `cli.ts run --suite <suite>` |
| `test-models.yml` | `cli.ts judge <results dir>` |
| `test-throughput.yml` | `cli.ts bench-throughput` |
| `test-context.yml` | `cli.ts bench-context` |
| `test-mcp.yml` | `cli.ts test-mcp` |
| `test-report-sweep.yml` | `cli.ts bench-throughput` · `test-mcp` · `model-bounds` |
| `test-pipeline.yml` | build → runtime → inference → models |

## 2. Folder → command

![Each cicd folder and the command that uses it](../docs/diagrams/png/cicd-folders.png)

Run these from `cicd/tests/`:

| Folder | Holds | Command |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/testcases/<suite>/` | one YAML per testcase | `npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite <suite> [--id <TC-ID>] [--dry-run]` |
| `tests/src/` | CLI, executor, log collector, judges | `npx tsc --noEmit` |
| `tests/.env.example` | config for a run outside CI | `cp .env.example .env` |
| `tests/scripts/` | runner helpers | `npx tsx scripts/validate-agent-judge.ts` |
| `scripts/` | tools the workflows call | `python3 ../scripts/scrub-session-log.py scan <log.jsonl>` |
| `results/` | run output, gitignored | written by `run`; `--output-dir <dir>` overrides |
| `specs/` · `infrastructure/` | notes | — |

Pass `--format json` to `run` or `judge` to print the summary as JSON.

## 3. The host decides the server under test

![Runner .env knobs, their defaults, and host B's values](../docs/diagrams/png/cicd-host-env.png)

A self-hosted runner reads its own `.env` (in the runner's folder), so each host names its server without a workflow edit. An unset knob takes the default from `cicd/tests/src/config.ts` or the workflow step.

| Knob | Default | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `OLLAMA37_CONTAINER` | `ollama37` | testcase steps, log collector |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | `http://localhost:11434` | testcase steps, perf commands, workflow steps |
| `OLLAMA37_TEST_IDS` | unset: every test | `cli.ts run` |
| `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` | unset: no service switch | `test-models.yml` |
| `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE` | unset | `test-models.yml` |

For a local run, set them in `cicd/tests/.env` or on the command line:

```bash
OLLAMA37_CONTAINER=ollama37-3060 npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models --id TC-MODELS-003
```

## 4. A models run on a shared host

![Yield GPU, run tests, restore GPU, then the agent judge](../docs/diagrams/png/cicd-models-flow.png)

On a host whose runner sets `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, `test-models.yml` stops `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE` and starts `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` as user systemd units. It then runs the tests with the simple judge and saves `results.json`. Afterwards it restores the yielded service if that service is enabled, and only then runs the agent judge on the saved results. On a host without `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` the switch steps skip.

The same split by hand:

```bash
JUDGE_MODE=simple npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models --output-dir ../results/models
JUDGE_MODE=dual   npx tsx src/cli.ts judge ../results/models
```

Run one job at a time on a host with more than one runner: its test services share port 11434.

## Diagrams

The PNGs are rendered from `docs/diagrams/*.svg`:

```bash
docs/diagrams/render.sh
```

**PASS**, after one round of fixes: the new `cicd/README.md` (650 words) passes the `review-readme` gate. Every command, path, env var and link in it was checked against the code. Both commit-related items are still open (see the end).

**Finding:** the first gate said REVISE, and I fixed all of it in the README and diagrams I'd just written:

| Line | Finding | Fix applied |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 4 intro sentences: passive voice, "no longer", "cannot … without", a leading "So" | rewritten in the active voice and without negatives |
| old 5–18 | Quick start sat between the intro and key point 1 | moved after key point 4 (now line 74) |
| 61 | "Afterwards" filler; the **Unload** step from the code was missing | "It unloads the test models, restores…"; the flow diagram now shows it too |
| 61, 42 | 3 more sentences with negatives or a buried subject | rewritten |
| 71 | the one-job-at-a-time rule had no weight | now **bold** |
| 89 | passive "The PNGs are rendered…" | "`docs/diagrams/render.sh` renders…" |

I kept the tables that repeat the diagrams on purpose: an agent can copy text from a table, not from a PNG.

## What was built

- **README:** SCQA opening, then the four key points, each with its PNG:
  1. One runner, three layers
  2. Folder → command
  3. The host decides the server under test
  4. A models run on a shared host

  Quick start and Diagrams come after them.
- **`docs/diagrams/`:** four `cicd-*.svg` files with their `png/` renders, plus `render.sh` (`rsvg-convert -z 2`). The PNGs re-render byte-identical.
- **Sources for this year's README conventions:** [AGENTS.md guide 2026](https://blog.buildbetter.ai/agents-md-complete-guide-for-engineering-teams-in-2026/), [AGENTS.md spec 2026](https://www.morphllm.com/agents-md-guide), [Red Hat: project context with AGENTS.md](https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2026/07/27/standardize-project-context-agentsmd-and-agent-skills), [GitHub README best practices 2026](https://pushpen.dev/blog/github-readme-best-practices-2026), [README template guide 2026](https://gingiris.github.io/growth-tools/blog/2026/04/02/github-readme-template-guide/).

**Still open:**
- **Nothing is committed.** Review step 5 expects committed PNGs, and `docs/diagrams/` and the new README are both untracked on `fix-513-host-env`.
- **Links elsewhere.** A few pages outside `cicd/` may still point at the deleted `cicd/docs/`. I didn't check them.

**Next step:** tell me whether to commit the branch now (code + README + diagrams). The alternative is to wait for the runner registration and a CI run on `sm86` first.

fix(#513): read the server under test from the host, and let a shared host lend a GPU

The models suite followed the server log through `docker compose logs`, so a
container started any other way lost its log, and every suite hard-coded the
container name and address.

- cicd/tests/src/config.ts sets OLLAMA37_CONTAINER (ollama37) and OLLAMA_HOST
  (http://localhost:11434) unless the environment already does; a self-hosted
  runner's .env overrides them per host.
- The log collector follows `docker logs --follow $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER`, stdout
  and stderr merged, however the container was started.
- All testcases use $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER and $OLLAMA_HOST; workflows drop the
  job-level OLLAMA_HOST so the runner's .env wins; compose reads container_name.
- OLLAMA37_TEST_IDS limits `cli.ts run` to a host's subset.
- `cli.ts run` saves results.json; `cli.ts judge <dir>` judges it later.
- test-models.yml: Yield GPU / Restore GPU switch OLLAMA37_SERVICE and
  OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE (user systemd units) around the run, and the agent
  judge runs after the restore. Hosts that set neither skip both steps.

Verified on host B (RTX 3060): TC-MODELS-003 passed both judges through the
yield -> run -> restore -> judge sequence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <[REDACTED-email]>
EOF

The models suite keeps each test's server log for the report and the agent judge, and every suite reaches the server by container name and address. The testbeds now include a second host that starts its ollama37 container from a systemd unit, pinned to one card, and whose GPUs also serve the agent judge. Its runs lost the server log, because the collector only read `docker compose logs`, and every hard-coded `ollama37` and `localhost:11434` pointed at the wrong server. The pipeline now reads its server under test from each runner's `.env`, follows the container's log by name, and on a shared host lends a card to the test and returns it before judging.

Refs #513. This PR does not close it: the compose-started run on the K80 host is still to verify.

## Details

- **Host knobs:** `cicd/tests/src/config.ts` sets `OLLAMA37_CONTAINER` (`ollama37`) and `OLLAMA_HOST` (`http://localhost:11434`) unless the environment does. A runner's `.env` overrides them per host, so host A needs no change.
- **Log collector:** follows `docker logs --follow $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER`, stdout and stderr merged into one ordered stream, however the container was started.
- **Testcases:** every suite uses `$OLLAMA37_CONTAINER` (48 places) and `$OLLAMA_HOST` (90). TC-RUNTIME-001 drops its container-name pattern; `compose ps` already scopes to the project.
- **Workflows:** the job-level `OLLAMA_HOST` is removed so the runner's `.env` wins; shell steps fall back with `${VAR:-default}`. `test-mlx-smoke.yml` stops and starts the production container by `OLLAMA37_CONTAINER`.
- **Subset:** `OLLAMA37_TEST_IDS` limits `cli.ts run` to a host's testcases.
- **Tests before judge:** `cli.ts run` saves `results.json`, and the new `cli.ts judge <dir>` judges it in a later step.
- **Shared host (`test-models.yml`):** Yield GPU stops `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE` and starts `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` (user systemd units). Restore GPU (`always()`) gives the card back if the yielded service is enabled, and the agent judge then runs on the saved results. Hosts that set neither key skip both steps.
- **Docs:** `cicd/docs/` is removed; the rewritten `cicd/README.md` maps folder → command → host knobs, with SVG sources in `docs/diagrams/` and `docs/diagrams/render.sh`.
- **Verified:** on host B (RTX 3060), TC-MODELS-003 passed both judges through yield → run → unload → restore → judge, run by hand with the runner's `.env`. Type check clean; all YAML parses; README commands, paths, env vars and links checked against the code.
- **Not verified:** a compose-started run on host A (offline), and a CI run on host B (its runner is not registered yet).
- **Known gap:** on the GTX 1080 Ti the die check fails `GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED`, because a second 99 MiB compute process sits on that card. The 3060 passes.

message.content: give me the command that down and up service

content.text:
They're all user services, so `systemctl --user`, no sudo.

**Switch to the 3060 test server** (what Yield GPU does):
```bash
systemctl --user stop ollama
systemctl --user start ollama37-3060
```

**Switch back to the judge server** (what Restore GPU does):
```bash
systemctl --user stop ollama37-3060
systemctl --user start ollama
```

**One service on its own:**
```bash
systemctl --user stop ollama37-3060        # down
systemctl --user start ollama37-3060       # up
systemctl --user restart ollama37-3060     # down + up, e.g. after changing the image
systemctl --user status ollama37-3060      # check
```

For the 1080 Ti, swap `3060` for `1080ti`. Only one of `ollama`, `ollama37-3060` and `ollama37-1080ti` can run at a time, since they share port 11434.

If you edit a unit file first (for example to change the image), run `systemctl --user daemon-reload` before `restart`.

```bash
systemctl --user daemon-reload
```

```bash
install -m 644 ~/src/ollama37/actions-runner-3060.service ~/.config/systemd/user/

systemctl --user restart actions-runner-3060
```

```bash
systemctl --user cat ollama37-3060
```

Every workflow is dispatched to a self-hosted GPU testbed by its `runner_label` input, and since #515 each runner's own `.env` decides the server it tests. The testbeds changed: host B now carries two runners, `sm61` (GTX 1080 Ti) and `sm86` (RTX 3060), and the RTX 2060 behind `sm75` is gone. `runner_label` is a `choice` input whose options are written into each workflow file, so GitHub refuses the new labels (`HTTP 422: Provided value 'sm86' for input 'runner_label' not in the list of allowed values`), still offers the retired `sm75`, and adding, removing or relabelling a runner means editing every workflow. Resolving it means a runner change reaches dispatch without touching the workflow files.

Context: [`.sessions/cf5a3839-e080-4036-9e9c-69476f9a0c27.jsonl`](../blob/main/.sessions/cf5a3839-e080-4036-9e9c-69476f9a0c27.jsonl)

The same input in all 11 workflows under `.github/workflows/`: `runner_label: type: choice, options: [sm37, sm75]`, default `sm37`.

`release-docker.yml` · `test-build.yml` · `test-context.yml` · `test-inference.yml` · `test-mcp.yml` · `test-mlx-smoke.yml` · `test-models.yml` · `test-pipeline.yml` · `test-report-sweep.yml` · `test-runtime.yml` · `test-throughput.yml`

## Runners today

| Runner | Labels | Host |
|---|---|---|
| `rocky8-k80-cicd-1` | `sm37` | host A (Tesla K80) |
| `rocky9-1080ti-cicd-1` | `sm61` | host B (GTX 1080 Ti) |
| `rocky9-3060-cicd-1` | `sm86` | host B (RTX 3060) |

No runner carries `sm75`.

## Seen

`gh workflow run test-models.yml -f runner_label=sm86 -f test_id=TC-MODELS-016` → HTTP 422, no run created.

## Open

Where the list of runners should live is undecided. The reporter leans toward a GitHub-side setting rather than a list written into the workflow files.

## Done When

- [ ] A workflow can be dispatched to `sm61` and `sm86`.
- [ ] Adding, removing or relabelling a runner needs no edit to the workflow files.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about your query regarding dynamic workflow_dispatch choice input options in GitHub Actions.

## Key Findings

**Dynamic Options Not Natively Supported**: GitHub Actions does not currently support populating workflow_dispatch input values dynamically using API responses or GitHub workflow outputs with expressions in the YAML configuration. Users have requested this feature, but it has been placed on GitHub's backlog.

**Workarounds for Dynamic Options**:

1. **GitHub Action-based Solutions**: There are GitHub Actions available that can dynamically add, update, or delete choices from workflow_dispatch input options in repository workflows. For example, the `dynamic-workflow-choices` action can modify workflow files before execution.

2. **YAML File Generation**: To have dynamically generated choice parameters displayed in a drop-down menu, you can create a GitHub Action that updates the parameters in the YAML file of the main action whenever changes are pushed.

3. **Template Substitution**: Some users utilize template substitution with tools like `envsubst` to replace placeholder content with dynamically generated option lists before the workflow runs.

**Current Limitations**: GitHub does not support using variable expressions (like `${{ vars.* }}`) or environment variables directly in the `options` field of workflow_dispatch choice inputs—these must be hardcoded static values in the YAML file at definition time.

Step 3, the report.

**REVISE**: a GitHub variable **can't fill the dropdown**, but it can be the runner list if the input becomes free text that's checked against the variable.

**Finding:**
- **`options:` can't read a variable.** In `on.workflow_dispatch.inputs.<id>.options`, GitHub evaluates no contexts (no `vars`, no `secrets`), so the choices must be literal YAML. GitHub's contexts table lists no context for that key, and the feature request has been on GitHub's backlog for years ([contexts reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts), [community #12029](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/12029)).
- **The known workarounds rewrite the workflow files** (e.g. [dynamic-workflow-choices](https://github.com/allankp/dynamic-workflow-choices), generated YAML). That fails #516's second Done When item.
- **A variable does work where the job is placed.** `jobs.<id>.runs-on` and `jobs.<id>.if` can both read `vars` and `inputs`.
- **Use a variable, not a secret.** Secrets can't be read in `runs-on` or `if`, and runner labels aren't secret.

**What does work with a variable:**

| Piece | Setting |
|---|---|
| Repo variable | `RUNNER_LABELS` = `["sm37","sm61","sm86"]` (repo-level, so `runs-on` can read it before any environment applies) |
| Input | `runner_label: type: string, default: "sm37"` (free text instead of a dropdown) |
| Guard | a small preflight job on a GitHub-hosted runner fails fast unless `contains(fromJSON(vars.RUNNER_LABELS), inputs.runner_label)`, and prints the valid list |
| Placement | unchanged: `runs-on: [self-hosted, "${{ inputs.runner_label }}"]` |

Adding, removing or relabelling a runner is then `gh variable set RUNNER_LABELS --body '[…]'`, with no file edit. The cost is losing the dropdown: you type the label, and a typo fails in seconds instead of hanging on a runner that never comes. The `default:` of a dispatch input can't read `vars` either, so `sm37` stays written in the file.

**Recommend:** the string input with the variable guard. It meets both Done When items; the only other way is file rewriting, which breaks the second.

**Next step:** confirm this design, and I'll implement it across the 11 workflows on a branch and create `RUNNER_LABELS`. Creating the repo variable changes GitHub settings, so I'll ask before running that command.

content.content:
```yaml
runs-on: [self-hosted, sm37]      # Tesla K80 — the only hardware-validated target
```

| Label | Host | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sm37` | Tesla K80 box (`rocky9-k80-cicd-1`) | 4 dies, ~11.4 GiB each. The reference testbed. |
| `sm75` | RTX 2060 box (`rocky9-2060-cicd-1`) | 1 card, **5.1 GiB usable** (display attached). |

A workflow that can run on more than one testbed takes a `runner_label` input defaulting to
`sm37`, and uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, "${{ inputs.runner_label || 'sm37' }}"]`.

**Not every suite fits every host.** `sm75` holds no model the `models` suite uses
(`deepseek-r1:32b`, `gemma3:27b`, …), and the `build` suite is a multi-hour no-cache compile that
belongs on `sm37` where the builder image is cached. The `runtime` suite needs no model and runs
anywhere.

**Order of operations when adding a runner:** add the label to the runner *first*, then pin
workflows to it. Pinning to a label no runner carries makes every job queue forever.

**Identify the host** as the first step after checkout, so a result is attributable to a
testbed rather than to "self-hosted":
=====
whether it passed or failed): `gh run view <build-run> --log | grep 'retagged sha256'`. No match →
the recreate, and every test after it, silently exercises stale code.

```bash
gh workflow run test-runtime.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=<sm37|sm75>
```

- **`runner_label`** — which box: `sm37` (`rocky9-k80-cicd-1`, the reference K80 testbed) or `sm75`
  (`rocky9-2060-cicd-1`, RTX 2060). Default `sm37`. Never a bare `runs-on: self-hosted` — a K80 sweep on
  a consumer card produces numbers that look valid and are not.
- **`--ref <branch>`** — check out that branch's `docker-compose.yml` and testcases. Omit for the
  default branch.

Never `docker compose up`/`down` yourself to apply an image — run the runtime workflow so the recreate
is logged and reproducible.
=====
tag **`ollama37:latest`** on the runner it ran on.

```bash
gh workflow run test-build.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=<sm37|sm75>
gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status        # block until done; GitHub holds the logs
```

- **`runner_label`** — which box: `sm37` (`rocky9-k80-cicd-1`, 4× K80) or `sm75` (`rocky9-2060-cicd-1`,
  RTX 2060). Default `sm37`. Never a bare `runs-on: self-hosted`.
- **`--ref <branch>`** — which code. Omit to build the default branch.
- The build normally runs on **`sm37`** (its ~15 GB builder image is cached there; on a fresh host
  `ensure-builder` rebuilds it, ~90 min). It can run on `sm75` only if `ollama37-builder:latest` is
  already present there.

## The CI image lands where compose reads it — same host, no push
=====

## Run one

```bash
gh workflow run test-throughput.yml --ref <branch> \
  -f runner_label=sm75 \
  -f models=<model> \
  -f flash_attention=<0|1> \
  -f kv_cache_type='' \
  -f context_size=8192 -f num_predict=128 \
  -f judge_mode=dual
gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status
```

Read the markdown table in the run summary: **Prompt tok/s** = prefill, **Gen tok/s** = decode,
**Check** = PASS/FAIL (the judge's verdict). Collect one row per path and compare.

## The testbed reverts itself — fail is data

`test-throughput.yml` is self-contained: it applies the experiment env by recreating the container,
benchmarks, and in an `always()` step **reverts to the stable baseline (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0`)**.
So a kernel that panics — e.g. tensor-core MMA on Turing under CUDA 11.4 — is a *recorded result*
("unusable"), and the testbed is still left clean for the next run. Never chase a green result by
dodging the crash; the crash is the finding.

`models` is `sm37`-only for the large models; on `sm75` size to the ~5 GiB it has.

## Size a model's context/batch fit (fit-map sweep)
=====
intent:
  user_story: |
    Verify the GPU is detected by nvidia-smi and the Ollama CUDA runtime.
  notes: |
    Host-agnostic: runs on any GPU testbed (sm37 = Tesla K80, sm75 = RTX 2060, …).
    Asserts the property "a CUDA GPU is present and in use", not a specific card,
    driver, or compute capability — the identify-host action records those per run.

=================== ollama37-ci-apply
SKILL.md
     1	---
     2	name: ollama37-ci-apply
     3	description: Apply a built ollama37 image onto a testbed through CI — recreate the container, never docker compose by hand
     4	user-invocable: true
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Apply the ollama37 image with CI
     8	
     9	Roll a freshly built image onto a testbed through the GitHub Actions runtime workflow on a self-hosted
    10	runner — never `docker compose up` or `docker exec` on a dev box. To *build* the image first, see
    11	`ollama37-ci-build`.
    12	
    13	$ARGUMENTS
    14	
    15	## Applying = running the runtime workflow
    16	
    17	**`test-runtime.yml` is how a built image is applied.** `TC-RUNTIME-001` runs `docker compose down`
    18	then `docker compose up -d`, which recreates the container from **`dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`** — the
    19	tag `docker-compose.yml` reads. The `ollama-data` volume is `external`, so pulled models survive the
    20	recreate. The same run then exercises the runtime checks (startup, GPU detection, health).
    21	
    22	**Precondition — confirm the retag, or you apply a STALE image.** The build produces `ollama37:latest`;
    23	only **`TC-BUILD-004`** retags it to `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest` (the tag compose reads). So apply
    24	picks up your fresh build *only if the build ran that retag*. A full `test-build.yml` run does (TC-BUILD-004 runs in the build suite) — but a single-test build
    25	(`-f test_id=TC-BUILD-002`) **skips it**, leaving
    26	the compose tag pointing at the previous image. **Before applying, confirm the retag actually
    27	succeeded** — grep the build run for TC-BUILD-004's success line, not just its name (the name appears
    28	whether it passed or failed): `gh run view <build-run> --log | grep 'retagged sha256'`. No match →
    29	the recreate, and every test after it, silently exercises stale code.
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	gh workflow run test-runtime.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37
    33	```
    34	
    35	- **`runner_label`** — which box: `sm37` (`rocky8-k80-cicd-1`, the reference K80 testbed). Default
    36	  `sm37`. `sm61` and `sm86` (host B) run the `models` suite only; the runtime recreate is not set up there. Never a bare `runs-on: self-hosted` — a K80 sweep on
    37	  a consumer card produces numbers that look valid and are not.
    38	- **`--ref <branch>`** — check out that branch's `docker-compose.yml` and testcases. Omit for the
    39	  default branch.
    40	
    41	Never `docker compose up`/`down` yourself to apply an image — run the runtime workflow so the recreate
    42	is logged and reproducible.
    43	
    44	## Where apply fits
    45	
    46	`ollama37-ci-build` builds the image; this skill applies it; then the test suites
    47	(`test-models.yml`, etc.) exercise it. `test-pipeline.yml` chains `build → runtime → inference →
    48	models` for one `runner_label` if you want the whole flow in one run — and because the build suite
    49	retags the fresh image to the tag compose reads (`TC-BUILD-004`, see `ollama37-ci-build`), that one
    50	pipeline run builds *and* applies the new bits. Testing is **single-host**; the retired cross-host
    51	by-digest path no longer applies.
=================== ollama37-ci-build
SKILL.md
     1	---
     2	name: ollama37-ci-build
     3	description: Build the ollama37 CI image on a self-hosted GPU runner — never with a local make
     4	user-invocable: true
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Build the ollama37 CI image with CI
     8	
     9	Build the fork's runtime image through the GitHub Actions build workflow on a self-hosted runner —
    10	`gh workflow run`, never `make build-runtime-local` on a dev box. To *apply* a built image to a
    11	testbed, see `ollama37-ci-apply`.
    12	
    13	$ARGUMENTS
    14	
    15	## Never build by hand — a local build is version-crippled
    16	
    17	A local `make` build defaults `OLLAMA_VERSION=0.0.0` (`docker/Makefile`), and the ollama registry
    18	rejects every gated model pull from an old version with `412: requires a newer version` — so the image
    19	*looks* fine and silently cannot pull modern models (qwen3.5, gemma3, ministral-3, …). The CI build
    20	injects `OLLAMA_VERSION` from the **repo variable** (check it: `gh variable list`), which is `>` any
    21	`0.x` minimum and clears the gate. Only the CI image can pull those models. It also leaves logs; a hand
    22	`make` leaves nothing.
    23	
    24	## The build
    25	
    26	**`TC-BUILD-002` IS the build** — `test-build.yml` runs `make build-runtime-local-no-cache`, a full
    27	no-cache compile (preset "CUDA 11 K80", native CUBIN sm_37…sm_86, no GPU needed). It produces the local
    28	tag **`ollama37:latest`** on the runner it ran on.
    29	
    30	```bash
    31	gh workflow run test-build.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37
    32	gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status        # block until done; GitHub holds the logs
    33	```
    34	
    35	- **`runner_label`** — which box: `sm37` (`rocky8-k80-cicd-1`, 4× K80). Default `sm37`. `sm61` and
    36	  `sm86` (host B) run the `models` suite only. Never a bare `runs-on: self-hosted`.
    37	- **`--ref <branch>`** — which code. Omit to build the default branch.
    38	- The build normally runs on **`sm37`** (its ~15 GB builder image is cached there; on a fresh host
    39	  `ensure-builder` rebuilds it, ~90 min).
    40	
    41	## The CI image lands where compose reads it — same host, no push
    42	
    43	The build produces the local tag **`ollama37:latest`**, but `docker/docker-compose.yml` reads
    44	**`dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`**. `TC-BUILD-004` (in the build suite) bridges that gap: it retags the
    45	fresh `ollama37:latest` → `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest` **locally**, so every later `docker compose up`
    46	(runtime/inference/models/perf) exercises the build we just made — no compose edit, no Docker Hub push.
    47	
    48	**A single-test build skips the retag.** `TC-BUILD-004` only runs as part of the full build suite. If
    49	you build one test (`-f test_id=TC-BUILD-002`), `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest` still points at the
    50	*previous* image — so apply + every downstream test silently exercises stale code. Run the full
    51	`test-build.yml` (no `test_id`), or run the retag too (`-f test_id=TC-BUILD-004`). `ollama37-ci-apply` restates this as a
    52	precondition to confirm before applying.
    53	
    54	This is **single-host**: build and test on the same runner. The old cross-host path — publish to
    55	`dogkeeper886/ollama37-ci:ci-<sha>` and pull by digest on a second card — was **retired** (#441): the
    56	push was slow and nothing ever consumed the pushed image. To restore the *published* image on a runner
    57	(e.g. for a published-image baseline), `docker pull dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`.
    58	
    59	Once built, hand off to `ollama37-ci-apply` to roll it onto the testbed.
=================== ollama37-ci-perf
SKILL.md
     1	---
     2	name: ollama37-ci-perf
     3	description: Run a decision-grade FA/CUDA performance experiment via CI — verified throughput, self-reverting testbed
     4	user-invocable: true
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Run an ollama37 performance experiment with CI
     8	
     9	Measure a CUDA / flash-attention change's real performance through `test-throughput.yml` on a
    10	self-hosted runner — tok/s that can actually decide whether to keep or drop the change. Build the
    11	variant under test with `ollama37-ci-build`; apply an image with `ollama37-ci-apply`.
    12	
    13	$ARGUMENTS
    14	
    15	## Decision-grade, or it doesn't count
    16	
    17	Raw tok/s from a hand `curl` loop is **not** evidence for an FA decision — it is single-run and never
    18	checks the answer is correct; a path that is faster but emits garbage is not a win. Decision-grade
    19	means all three:
    20	
    21	- **Verified response** — `judge_mode=dual` runs the keyless agent judge for *meaningfulness*, not
    22	  just "non-empty." Required for any keep/drop decision. **`dual` silently degrades to `simple` if the
    23	  runner has no agent-judge auth (`~/.claude`)** — so confirm a judge *verdict* actually appears in the
    24	  run; if it fell back to `simple`, the response is not verified and the number is not decision-grade.
    25	- **Realistic context** — `context_size` ≥ ~6.8k, not a one-line prompt. A short prompt once hid a
    26	  7.4× flash-attention regression on the K80 behind a 22% one (`docs/porting-k80.md` §3).
    27	- **Consistent** — the workflow recreates the container per run, so the state is fixed; compare paths
    28	  on the same model + context.
    29	
    30	## A "path" is (build) × (runtime env)
    31

# Apply the ollama37 image with CI

Roll a freshly built image onto a testbed through the GitHub Actions runtime workflow on a self-hosted
runner — never `docker compose up` or `docker exec` on a dev box. To *build* the image first, see
`ollama37-ci-build`.

$ARGUMENTS

## Applying = running the runtime workflow

**`test-runtime.yml` is how a built image is applied.** `TC-RUNTIME-001` runs `docker compose down`
then `docker compose up -d`, which recreates the container from **`dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`** — the
tag `docker-compose.yml` reads. The `ollama-data` volume is `external`, so pulled models survive the
recreate. The same run then exercises the runtime checks (startup, GPU detection, health).

**Precondition — confirm the retag, or you apply a STALE image.** The build produces `ollama37:latest`;
only **`TC-BUILD-004`** retags it to `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest` (the tag compose reads). So apply
picks up your fresh build *only if the build ran that retag*. A full `test-build.yml` run does (TC-BUILD-004 runs in the build suite) — but a single-test build
(`-f test_id=TC-BUILD-002`) **skips it**, leaving
the compose tag pointing at the previous image. **Before applying, confirm the retag actually
succeeded** — grep the build run for TC-BUILD-004's success line, not just its name (the name appears
whether it passed or failed): `gh run view <build-run> --log | grep 'retagged sha256'`. No match →
the recreate, and every test after it, silently exercises stale code.

```bash
gh workflow run test-runtime.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37
```

- **`runner_label`** — which box: `sm37` (`rocky8-k80-cicd-1`, the reference K80 testbed). Default
  `sm37`. `sm61` and `sm86` (host B) run the `models` suite only; the runtime recreate is not set up there. Never a bare `runs-on: self-hosted` — a K80 sweep on
  a consumer card produces numbers that look valid and are not.
- **`--ref <branch>`** — check out that branch's `docker-compose.yml` and testcases. Omit for the
  default branch.

Never `docker compose up`/`down` yourself to apply an image — run the runtime workflow so the recreate
is logged and reproducible.

## Where apply fits

`ollama37-ci-build` builds the image; this skill applies it; then the test suites
(`test-models.yml`, etc.) exercise it. `test-pipeline.yml` chains `build → runtime → inference →
models` for one `runner_label` if you want the whole flow in one run — and because the build suite
retags the fresh image to the tag compose reads (`TC-BUILD-004`, see `ollama37-ci-build`), that one
pipeline run builds *and* applies the new bits. Testing is **single-host**; the retired cross-host
by-digest path no longer applies.

# Build the ollama37 CI image with CI

Build the fork's runtime image through the GitHub Actions build workflow on a self-hosted runner —
`gh workflow run`, never `make build-runtime-local` on a dev box. To *apply* a built image to a
testbed, see `ollama37-ci-apply`.

$ARGUMENTS

## Never build by hand — a local build is version-crippled

A local `make` build defaults `OLLAMA_VERSION=0.0.0` (`docker/Makefile`), and the ollama registry
rejects every gated model pull from an old version with `412: requires a newer version` — so the image
*looks* fine and silently cannot pull modern models (qwen3.5, gemma3, ministral-3, …). The CI build
injects `OLLAMA_VERSION` from the **repo variable** (check it: `gh variable list`), which is `>` any
`0.x` minimum and clears the gate. Only the CI image can pull those models. It also leaves logs; a hand
`make` leaves nothing.

## The build

**`TC-BUILD-002` IS the build** — `test-build.yml` runs `make build-runtime-local-no-cache`, a full
no-cache compile (preset "CUDA 11 K80", native CUBIN sm_37…sm_86, no GPU needed). It produces the local
tag **`ollama37:latest`** on the runner it ran on.

```bash
gh workflow run test-build.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37
gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status        # block until done; GitHub holds the logs
```

- **`runner_label`** — which box: `sm37` (`rocky8-k80-cicd-1`, 4× K80). Default `sm37`. `sm61` and
  `sm86` (host B) run the `models` suite only. Never a bare `runs-on: self-hosted`.
- **`--ref <branch>`** — which code. Omit to build the default branch.
- The build normally runs on **`sm37`** (its ~15 GB builder image is cached there; on a fresh host
  `ensure-builder` rebuilds it, ~90 min).

## The CI image lands where compose reads it — same host, no push

The build produces the local tag **`ollama37:latest`**, but `docker/docker-compose.yml` reads
**`dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`**. `TC-BUILD-004` (in the build suite) bridges that gap: it retags the
fresh `ollama37:latest` → `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest` **locally**, so every later `docker compose up`
(runtime/inference/models/perf) exercises the build we just made — no compose edit, no Docker Hub push.

**A single-test build skips the retag.** `TC-BUILD-004` only runs as part of the full build suite. If
you build one test (`-f test_id=TC-BUILD-002`), `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest` still points at the
*previous* image — so apply + every downstream test silently exercises stale code. Run the full
`test-build.yml` (no `test_id`), or run the retag too (`-f test_id=TC-BUILD-004`). `ollama37-ci-apply` restates this as a
precondition to confirm before applying.

This is **single-host**: build and test on the same runner. The old cross-host path — publish to
`dogkeeper886/ollama37-ci:ci-<sha>` and pull by digest on a second card — was **retired** (#441): the
push was slow and nothing ever consumed the pushed image. To restore the *published* image on a runner
(e.g. for a published-image baseline), `docker pull dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`.

Once built, hand off to `ollama37-ci-apply` to roll it onto the testbed.

# Run an ollama37 performance experiment with CI

Measure a CUDA / flash-attention change's real performance through `test-throughput.yml` on a
self-hosted runner — tok/s that can actually decide whether to keep or drop the change. Build the
variant under test with `ollama37-ci-build`; apply an image with `ollama37-ci-apply`.

$ARGUMENTS

## Decision-grade, or it doesn't count

Raw tok/s from a hand `curl` loop is **not** evidence for an FA decision — it is single-run and never
checks the answer is correct; a path that is faster but emits garbage is not a win. Decision-grade
means all three:

- **Verified response** — `judge_mode=dual` runs the keyless agent judge for *meaningfulness*, not
  just "non-empty." Required for any keep/drop decision. **`dual` silently degrades to `simple` if the
  runner has no agent-judge auth (`~/.claude`)** — so confirm a judge *verdict* actually appears in the
  run; if it fell back to `simple`, the response is not verified and the number is not decision-grade.
- **Realistic context** — `context_size` ≥ ~6.8k, not a one-line prompt. A short prompt once hid a
  7.4× flash-attention regression on the K80 behind a 22% one (`docs/porting-k80.md` §3).
- **Consistent** — the workflow recreates the container per run, so the state is fixed; compare paths
  on the same model + context.

## A "path" is (build) × (runtime env)

- **`--ref <branch>`** selects the *kernel routing* that got compiled — FA-off, all-VEC, decode-only,
  MMA-on, … — i.e. `ollama37-ci-build`'s output.
- **`flash_attention`** selects *FA vs the non-FA cuBLAS path* at runtime: `0` = cuBLAS baseline,
  `1` = FA. `kv_cache_type` is the other runtime knob.

## Run one

```bash
gh workflow run test-throughput.yml --ref <branch> \
  -f runner_label=sm37 \
  -f models=<model> \
  -f flash_attention=<0|1> \
  -f kv_cache_type='' \
  -f context_size=8192 -f num_predict=128 \
  -f judge_mode=dual
gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status
```

Read the markdown table in the run summary: **Prompt tok/s** = prefill, **Gen tok/s** = decode,
**Check** = PASS/FAIL (the judge's verdict). Collect one row per path and compare.

## The testbed reverts itself — fail is data

`test-throughput.yml` is self-contained: it applies the experiment env by recreating the container,
benchmarks, and in an `always()` step **reverts to the stable baseline (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0`)**.
So a kernel that panics — e.g. tensor-core MMA on Turing under CUDA 11.4 — is a *recorded result*
("unusable"), and the testbed is still left clean for the next run. Never chase a green result by
dodging the crash; the crash is the finding.

The perf workflows recreate the compose container, so they run on `sm37`; `sm61` and `sm86`
(host B) are set up for the `models` suite only.

## Size a model's context/batch fit (fit-map sweep)

A different question from "is this FA path faster": *at what context does a model spill to CPU, and
does a smaller `num_batch` pull it back onto the GPU?* On the K80 (FA off) the `Q·Kᵀ` score buffer is
sized by `num_batch`, so batch — not just context — sets the VRAM wall. `test-report-sweep.yml` records
this as a **fit map** (the basis for the qwen35moe clamp in #440):

```bash
gh workflow run test-report-sweep.yml --ref <branch> \
  -f suite=none \
  -f fit_map_models='qwen3.6:35b' \
  -f fit_map_num_batches='512 256 128' \
  -f fit_map_contexts='8192 65536 98304 131072 196608 262144'
```

`suite=none` skips the default throughput/MCP sweeps so only the fit-map runs (the fit-map is
gated on `fit_map_models`, independent of `suite`). Per model it bounds the context ladder to the
trained window and gates on tool support (`cli.ts model-bounds`, via `/api/show`), then loops
`num_batch` x bounded-context. The
`report-sweep-results` artifact's `SUMMARY.md` holds the fit-map table: per cell the **fit**
(✅ on GPU / ⚠️ CPU spill / ❌ OOM), decode tok/s, `total_s`, per-die VRAM, active dies, and
offload% — captured from the MCP GPU snapshot **independent of the correctness verdict**, so a
judge hiccup never loses the fit data. Leave `fit_map_models` empty (default) and the sweep runs
its normal throughput/MCP pass unchanged.

content.text:
I restructured all three skills to the skill-structure rules; nothing is committed. Each file now has one frontmatter field (`description`), one header and one list, with no other lines (+39/−188 lines).

| Skill | Description (SCQA) | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama37-ci-apply` | hand `docker compose` → no log, and after a skipped retag it recreates the previous image → stale tests | 5: confirm the retag, stop and rerun `TC-BUILD-004` if it's missing, run `test-runtime.yml` on `sm37`, watch, test on the same label |
| `ollama37-ci-build` | local `make` → `OLLAMA_VERSION=0.0.0` → registry 412 → can't pull modern models | 5: check `OLLAMA_VERSION`, run the full `test-build.yml` on `sm37`, watch, confirm the retag, hand off to apply |
| `ollama37-ci-perf` | hand `curl` loop on a one-line prompt → no answer check, hid a 7.4× FA regression → the number can't decide | 7: build each path, run `test-throughput.yml` (8k context, `judge_mode=dual`), watch, confirm the judge verdict, record the three numbers, record a crash as unusable, compare |

**What the rewrite dropped:**
- **The fit-map sweep section in `ollama37-ci-perf`** (`test-report-sweep.yml`, `fit_map_models`, …). It answers a different question from the FA experiment, and one list can't hold two purposes. If you want to keep it, it would become its own skill.
- **The explanatory prose.** For example: why a local build is version-crippled, the retired cross-host publish path, what "decision-grade" means, and the `ollama-data` external volume. The steps keep the commands and checks; the reasons behind them are now only in each description.
- **`name` and `user-invocable` frontmatter.** Claude Code takes the name from the folder, and skills can be invoked by users by default, so `/ollama37-ci-apply` and the others should still work. I haven't tested that. `/reload-skills` would confirm it.

**PASS**: gemma4:e2b (`TC-MODELS-006`) passed on the RTX 3060 with both judges, in run [36299146873](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/36299146873). It loads **fully on the GPU**.

**Finding:**

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Placement | **36 of 36 layers on the RTX 3060** (35 repeating plus the output layer), 7706 MiB |
| Prefill | 29 tok in 18 ms = **1621 tok/s** |
| Decode | 126 tok in 1.0 s = **124 tok/s** |
| Raw response | `response: 2 plus 2 equals 4.` · `done_reason: stop`, `eval_count: 126` |
| Die check | `Active GPUs: 1` → `GPU_COUNT_OK` |
| Agent judge | PASS: loaded, readable text, no repeats, GPU memory 7706 MiB, unloaded |

That's **43× faster decode than gemma4:12b** (2.9 tok/s) on the same card. It shows what full placement is worth: the 12b's 7 CPU layers cost almost all of its speed. Both tests passed the suite, so only the placement line (`layers.offload` / `offloading N … layers`) tells a full load from a partial one.

The `single-gpu-load-test.md` row for gemma4:e2b already says "likely" for the 3060, and this run confirms it.

**Next step:** tell me the next model to run on the 3060.

content.text:
**FAILED**, but only on the die check. The model itself ran fine on the GTX 1080 Ti: `offloaded 36/36 layers to GPU`, 96 tok/s decode. The job failed because the check counted a second process on the card, as expected.

**Finding:**

| | GTX 1080 Ti (this run) | RTX 3060 (last run) |
|---|---|---|
| Placement | **36/36 layers on GPU** | 36/36 |
| Prefill | 29 tok in 28 ms = **1033 tok/s** | 1621 tok/s |
| Decode | 113 tok in 1.18 s = **96 tok/s** | 124 tok/s |
| Raw response | `Two plus two equals four.` · `done_reason: stop`, `eval_count: 113` | `2 plus 2 equals 4.` |
| Model VRAM | 7456 MiB | 7706 MiB |
| Die check | **`GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED`**, still after one reload | `GPU_COUNT_OK` |

**Why it failed:** `docker exec … nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` lists **pid 5813 using 111 MiB** alongside the model runner. The check counts each listed process as a GPU (`Active GPUs: 2`). So a model that fits one card is judged as spilling onto a second one. The simple judge failed on that, so the agent judge was skipped. Run: [36299330869](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/36299330869).

Pid 5813 is the same process as in the earlier local run. It isn't the model and it isn't ollama; the 1080 Ti drives the display, so it's probably a desktop process with a CUDA context. I haven't confirmed what it is.

**Recommend:** fix the check rather than the host. Counting distinct GPUs (`--query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid`) instead of processes would read 1 here. Counting only the model runner's own pid is another way. Either one keeps the K80's multi-die check intact.

**Next step:** tell me whether to identify pid 5813 first, or file the die-check fix as an issue.
